title: Divide Array Into Arrays With Max Difference
summary: Given an integer array nums with size n (n is a multiple of 3) and a positive integer k, divide nums into n/3 subarrays of size 3 such that the difference between any two elements in each subarray is no more than k.
statement: Given an integer array nums with size n (n is a multiple of 3) and a positive integer k, divide nums into n/3 subarrays of size 3 such that the difference between any two elements in each subarray is no more than k. Return a 2D array of these subarrays. If division is impossible, return an empty array. Multiple valid solutions are acceptable.
constraints: nums has positive length divisible by three and k is positive.
Return the canonical grouping made by sorting nums and taking consecutive triples.
Return an empty list if any triple maximum minus minimum exceeds k.
reference_solution:
def divide_into_bounded_triples(nums,k):
    nums=sorted(nums);answer=[]
    for index in range(0,len(nums),3):
        group=nums[index:index+3]
        if group[-1]-group[0]>k:return []
        answer.append(group)
    return answer

hints: In sorted order, the smallest remaining value must be grouped within the next two positions in any feasible partition.
Sort and partition consecutive blocks of three, rejecting any block whose endpoints differ by more than k.
For i=0,3,... take sorted_nums[i:i+3], test last-first, and append.
If a consecutive block fails, its smallest value cannot pair with two later values more closely; if all pass, the blocks directly witness feasibility.
